question.text: The tick size for stock options on NSE depends on:

answer.text: The price of the underlying stock: 0.01 paisa for stocks trading below Rs. 250, and 0.05 paisa for stocks trading above Rs. 250
A uniform Rs. 0.05 for all stock options regardless of underlying price
A uniform Rs. 0.01 for all stock options
The moneyness of the option: ITM options have smaller tick sizes

explanation.text: The Logic: Exchange contract specifications generally apply differentiated tick sizes based on the underlying's price level rather than a single uniform tick. In the standard NSE structure referenced in derivatives material, lower-priced underlyings carry a smaller minimum price increment (e.g., Rs. 0.01) and higher-priced underlyings carry a larger one (e.g., Rs. 0.05), with the Rs. 250 threshold as the dividing line. The other options posit a uniform tick or link it to option moneyness, neither of which matches exchange product specifications. The Trap: Tick size is set by the exchange in the contract specifications; it is not a uniform value across all contracts, and it is not driven by ITM/ATM/OTM status of the option. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook page (63) presents the differentiated tick-size structure in the context of stock futures, not stock options. The framing above generalises the NSE tick-size convention to the stock-options contract, which is not directly stated in the pages checked (63, 34); for an exam-grade answer the precise rule for stock options should be confirmed from the exchange product specification rather than from the cited workbook page.
